meta.title: Konta — accounting that does not need a programmer
meta.description: An accounting platform for companies and accounting firms in the Republic of Moldova. When the law changes, the update comes from us: no contractor, no reconfiguration. In development.

dev.text: Konta is being built right now. This page describes the product we are making and how far along it is, not one you could buy today.
hero.title: Accounting that does not need a programmer.
hero.lead: When the law changes, the update comes from us, the same day, for everybody. You open the program and get on with your work. No contractor, no reconfiguration, no waiting.
hero.soon: The app opens soon, to partner firms first.
vs.oldBody: Call the programmer, pay for the visit, wait. On every installation, every year.
vs.newBody: You do nothing. The new rate is already there when you open the program on Monday morning.
set.title: Fiscal rule set 2026
set.note: This is the file Konta takes its rates from. It is being checked by a licensed accountant and is not yet approved. Until it is, you can read and verify it yourself, one value at a time.
ef.title: The e-Factura mandate
ef.p1: Business-to-business electronic invoicing is scheduled to become mandatory on 1 October 2026, and a paper invoice loses its value for deducting VAT. If you are changing how you issue invoices anyway, this is the cheapest moment it will ever be.
ef.p2: Konta handles e-Factura for every client company from one screen, and purchase invoices that arrive as XML are posted automatically. The sales and purchase registers fill from what already went through SFS, not from what you re-typed.
ef.p3: The VAT refund ceiling was raised to 70% for taxpayers using e-Factura or MEV. That is a cash-flow gain you can calculate for each client individually.
ef.caveat: The 1 October 2026 date is reported by international VAT trackers. We are confirming it against the Moldovan legal act before treating it as settled, and will publish the answer here.
np.title: Why you will not need a programmer again
np.p1: In a program where the rules are written into the code, every change in the law means a paid person turning up to rewrite them, separately on every installation. In Konta the law sits as data: we change it once, for everyone. The 2027 fiscal reform has already passed its first reading — here is what it contains.
np.c1: New registration of Individual Enterprises and Peasant Farms closes
np.c2: Peasant farm income tax rises from 7% to 12%
np.c3: Dividend tax rises from 6% to 8% on profit earned after 2027
np.c4: The preferential small-trader rate rises from 1% to 3% of revenue
np.c5: CAEM revision 2.1 re-codes the activity classification of every entity
np.p2: Five rows, five reasons to call somebody out. For you, in Konta, they will be five rows that appear in the rulebook on their own, the same day, verifiable by anyone. You never pay for them: that is the whole idea of the product.
easy.title: Easy to work in, from the first day
easy.p1: Konta looks like a document, not like a database table. Open an invoice and you see an invoice. What has to be filled in is obvious; what calculates itself does not ask for your attention.
easy.p2: The interface is Romanian and Russian at parity, not half translated. The numpad keys you use in 1C stay the same, so ten years of reflexes are not lost in a week. The vocabulary is the SNC and the Fiscal Code, the words you say out loud, not a translation out of an American ERP.
easy.p3: And when something does not work, a person answers, on the telephone, in Romanian or Russian.
move.title: Moving off 1C
move.p1: Send us the database copy on Monday, work in Konta on Wednesday. We migrate the first company of any accounting firm ourselves, free; the second one you will do yourselves in a few hours.
move.p2: We run in parallel for as long as you need, so the switch rests on reconciled figures rather than on trust. We do not ask you to give anything up until you see the same totals in both programs.
part.title: We are looking for accounting firms who want to build this with us
part.p1: Konta is being made together with the people who will use it. If you run an accounting firm and are willing to work with us, you are welcome: you show us what eats your time today, we build around that, and you see the result before anyone else.
part.p2: What you get: the first company migrated by us, access to the product before launch, and the deciding word on what gets built next. What we ask: a few hours of your time, and honesty when something is not good.
part.p3: A quarter of an hour on the phone is enough to tell whether this makes sense for both of us.
open.title: Transparency
open.p1: We are asking you to trust us with payroll and with your clients' books. Here is what you can check yourself, without asking us.
open.b1: Anyone can read which rate we apply, from which date, and on the authority of which act. If a figure is wrong, it is visible from outside.
open.b2: The code that talks to SFS on your behalf can be read by anyone, line by line.
open.b3: Your data comes out in open formats, at any time, with no request and no fee. Leaving us should be as easy as joining.
open.b4: This page carries no analytics and no trackers. No request from your browser goes anywhere but konta.md, the fonts included.
contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: A person answers, in Romanian or Russian. If you are an accounting firm and the e-Factura mandate or a partnership is on your mind, call; the conversation takes a quarter of an hour.
